therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: glucose-dependent insulin secretion and glucagon suppression
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus on no medication or metformin only
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 16

results.effect_size: LS mean HbA1c change from baseline ranging from -0.25% (4 mg weekly) to -1.08% (30 mg weekly) vs -0.46% placebo; statistically significant differences vs placebo for 30 mg weekly (p=0.0027), 30 mg bi-weekly (p=0.0057), 50 mg bi-weekly (p=0.0032), and 100 mg every 4 weeks (p=0.0022)
results.target_engagement_evidence: EC50 for HbA1c ~1140-1230 ng/mL (treatment-naive and prior monotherapy groups); PK parameters: clearance 94.2 mL/hr, volume of distribution 16400 L, absorption rate 0.0193 hr^-1
biomarker_changes: Fasting plasma glucose reduced across active arms vs placebo at Week 16 (up to -1.44 mmol/L for 30 mg weekly)
Fasting fructosamine reduced across active arms (up to -38.1 µmol/L for 30 mg bi-weekly at Week 16)
Fasting glucagon reduced in most active arms
Fasting C-peptide changes variable across arms
Triglycerides reduced notably in 50 mg bi-weekly arm (up to -1.469 mmol/L at Week 16)
Total cholesterol modestly reduced in several arms
HDL-C and LDL-C changes small and inconsistent across arms
subgroup_findings: Treatment-naive group EC50 for HbA1c: 1140 ng/mL (95% CI 483-2990)
Prior monotherapy group EC50 for HbA1c: 1230 ng/mL (95% CI 403-3560)
Exenatide BID produced HbA1c reduction of -0.54% at Week 16 (unadjusted mean)
Higher albiglutide doses (30 mg weekly, 50 mg bi-weekly, 100 mg every 4 weeks) achieved greater HbA1c reductions than lower doses
safety_signals: Injection site reactions (erythema, hypersensitivity, pruritus, rash, urticaria) observed across multiple albiglutide arms
Serious cardiovascular events (angina pectoris, coronary artery disease, Prinzmetal angina) reported in individual patients across albiglutide arms
Gastric ulcer reported in one patient in 100 mg every 4 weeks arm
Exenatide BID associated with greater nausea/vomiting impact on quality of life (FLIE scores) compared to albiglutide arms
Albiglutide generally associated with less nausea/vomiting than exenatide BID based on FLIE questionnaire data

dose_info.dose: 4 mg, 15 mg, 30 mg, 50 mg, or 100 mg albiglutide; exenatide BID comparator
dose_info.schedule: Weekly, bi-weekly, or every 4 weeks subcutaneous injection for albiglutide; twice daily for exenatide

context.duration: 16 weeks treatment with follow-up to Week 27
